Executive Summary

Of the 28 active Neil sites (with all coordinate corrections applied), 15 are Tier 1 (strong Fresnel clearance through 10km), 6 are Tier 2 (directional issues requiring sector planning), 3 are Tier 3 (viable at 5km but not 10km), and 4 are Tier 4 (limited clearance).

The 15 Tier 1 sites carry 4,844 BSLs and should be prioritized for field validation. Tier 1+2 combined cover 7,099 BSLs (70%). Tier 1+2+3 reach 8,179 BSLs (81%).

Key concern: Phoenix Sonoran Preserve (1,110 BSLs) dropped to Tier 4 at its corrected location. This is the second-highest BSL site. The corrected coords place it in terrain that creates obstruction on multiple azimuths. This site needs drone LOS survey or alternative positioning to recover the BSL coverage.

Note: FSPL-only link budget shows negative margins beyond 5km, but does not account for Tarana's proprietary signal processing, beamforming gain, and interference mitigation which extend usable range well beyond free-space predictions. Field testing required to validate actual achievable range. The Fresnel zone analysis above (terrain clearance) remains the primary screening metric.

Methodology

  • Elevation data: SRTM1 (1 arc-second, ~30m resolution) from NASA/USGS
  • Path sampling: 16 radials x 5 distance bands (2, 4, 6, 8, 10 km) per site
  • Fresnel zone: First Fresnel zone radius calculated at each point along 200-point terrain profile
  • Classification: Clear LOS (100%+ F1), nLOS Adequate (60-100%), nLOS Marginal (0-60%), Obstructed (negative)
  • Tier assignment: Tier 1 (80%+ ext pass), Tier 2 (60-80%), Tier 3 (80%+ near only), Tier 4 (below thresholds)
  • BN antenna height: 30m AGL default, 39.6m (130 ft) Scottsdale Airport, 42.7m (140 ft) Falcon Field
  • RNm height: 5m AGL (rooftop mount)
